public_rationale: Zitron said Anthropic's annualized revenue claims don't line up with the 'exceeding $5 billion' lifetime revenue in the CFO's March 9 filing, because the annualized figures add up to over $6 billion. Anthropic's S-1 shows revenue of $41M (2023), $386M (2024) and $4,585M (2025), about $5.01B in total. That matches 'exceeding $5 billion' as a figure counted through year-end 2025. Actual revenue then kept pace with the run-rate claims: Q4 2025 was $2.04B, near what a $9B run-rate implies, and Q1 2026 alone was $4.73B. So real lifetime revenue was well above his $6B sum. The S-1 defines run-rate in an ordinary way. His adding-up was right; his conclusion that the numbers clash and point to an unusual definition was not.
limitations: The S-1 came out months after the post, so Zitron could not have seen it.
March 1–9, 2026 revenue is not broken out.

statement.excerpt: None of these numbers line up with previous statements about annualized revenue, by the way — I went into this last week — and no amount of contorting around the meaning of “exceeding” takes away from the fact that adding up all the annualized revenues is over $6 billion, which I believe means that Anthropic defines “annualized” in a new and innovative way.

None of these numbers line up with previous statements about annualized revenue
adding up all the annualized revenues is over $6 billion
which I believe means that Anthropic defines "annualized" in a new and innovative way
our_interpretation: Plain reading: Zitron says Anthropic's public annualized (run-rate) revenue figures from 2025 to early March 2026 do not fit the 'exceeding $5 billion' lifetime revenue in the March 9 declaration. Summing them gives over $6 billion, so he infers Anthropic's 'annualized' figures run ahead of real revenue under some unusual definition.

Following the reviewers, the test is not the word 'exceeding' alone. It is actual cumulative revenue, which the later S-1 reports. If actual recognized revenue through the period was well above $6 billion, the annualized statements did not run ahead of real revenue. Then the 'don't line up' claim and its 'new definition' inference fail.
The 'which I believe' clause is a hedged inference, but it rests on the factual claim of a mismatch. It is graded only through that claim.
criteria.support_condition: Anthropic's audited or reported revenue shows lifetime revenue through early March 2026 at or near $5 billion, well below what its run-rate statements implied. Or its disclosed run-rate method is unusual and inflates figures beyond recognized revenue.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Anthropic's reported revenue shows the 'exceeding $5 billion' figure matches recognized revenue through an earlier cut-off, and actual revenue by early 2026 was at or above what the run-rate statements implied, under a conventional run-rate definition.
